messages:
oliver: quick follow-up from the hot/cold lane prototype run this morning. put up a lightweight sketched PR and wanted to surface a few surprising tradeoffs we hit and get quick alignment.

oliver: tl;dr: separating enqueue into hot (short, low-token) vs cold (long-context/high-token) lanes reduced p99 latency for interactive tenants ~18% but increased tail kv-cache thrash and bursty gpu memory pressure for cold lane.

maya: nice! can you summarize the enqueue path changes? is it just a queue-per-length-bin or something else?

oliver: it's a dual-path. hot lane is a fast lock-free ring buffer that skips prefix prefetch and assumes no kv cache warmup. cold lane uses normal admission with prefetch + pinned kv reservations. we also added a lightweight length-hint header from the API to drive the decision.

kevin: length-hint seems reasonable but clients can lie. what happens on misclassification (hot declared but actually long)?

oliver: good call — we implemented a graceful fallback: if hot lane sees >max_tokens at dequeue, it requeues into cold lane and attaches a small penalty token to avoid oscillation. that path costs an extra enqueue/dequeue and sometimes misses early kv prefetch.

liz: how bad was the penalty in practice? numbers?

oliver: in 2h internal, for 200k requests: misclass rate ~0.7%, extra overhead per misclass ~4ms queuing + 8ms lost prefetch. overall net p50/p90 improved, p99 for tenants with many long requests actually worsened ~6% due to cache churn.

maya: cache churn = more eviction of kv pages because cold lane suddenly gets bursts? can we isolate caches by lane or tenant?

oliver: attempted per-lane kvcache namespaces in the prototype — reduces cross-lane eviction but doubles memory footprint which isn't acceptable for multi-tenant cards.

kevin: what about shared kvcache with lane-reservation tokens? e.g., cold lane can reserve eviction credits so we avoid evicting hot-page working sets.

oliver: we tried credits but hit fairness issues: a noisy tenant in cold lane hoards credits and starves others. credits + short window rebalancer helped but complexity exploded.

liz: any routing alternatives? dynamic batching already aggregates by seq len sometimes. Could we keep single queue but prioritize short jobs when latency SLO signals high?

oliver: yup — priority-aware coalescer was our second approach: single queue, but the dequeueer fast-path favors short requests if current latency budget tight. that preserved kvcache behavior but scheduling increased dequeue jitter and required more complex admission telemetry. net wins were smaller but operationally simpler.

maya: ops angle: do we get better observability with separate lanes? easier to attribute. but more knobs.

oliver: true. separate lanes give clear per-lane metrics (enq rate, misclass, queue depth) which made debugging faster in prototype.

ci-bot: perf-runner completed: 2026-03-21T09:12Z, suite: hot-cold-proto, p50_delta:-12.3%, p90_delta:-9.8%, p99_delta:+5.9%, kv_evictions:+22%

kevin: that's telling. +22% kv_evictions likely explains p99 bump. next steps?

oliver: proposal: merge the priority-aware single-queue approach into the scheduler as an experiment branch. keep the lane prototype as a gated option for customers who can pay for partitioned memory. action items: 1) add length-hint-sanitizer in API layer (maya) 2) telemetry dashboards for misclass + kv-evictions by tenant (liz) 3) implement dequeue-priority fastpath and run 24h A/B (kevin + oliver).

maya: can do api sanitizer. i'll add a fuzz test to simulate lying clients and ensure the penalty dampener avoids oscillation.

liz: i'll wire dashboards and add an alert if kv_evictions/rate exceeds threshold.

kevin: timeline?

oliver: aim for branch by EOW, start A/B next week.

maya: :thumbsup:

liz: :100:

kevin: sounds good — thanks for the clear writeup oliver.
